Classwork · Page 1 of 7

Lesson outcome

After this lesson you can describe a Russian holiday in five or six sentences and answer the exam question “What is your favourite public holiday? Why?”, using ready-made chunks instead of building every sentence word by word.

Warm-up. Which holiday do you look forward to most, and what exactly do you do on that day? Write two or three words, not a sentence.

Lexical approach: we learn whole chunks (put up a tree, lay flowers), not single words. A chunk is what you can say without thinking in the exam.

Classwork · Page 2 of 7

Step 1 · Input: three Russian holidays

First listen once with the text closed and answer the gist question: which three holidays are described? Then read.

Three Russian holidays
Read the text (after listening)

Russians celebrate a great many holidays, but three of them show the character of the country especially well.

New Year is the most popular holiday of the year. Families put up a decorated tree, cook a lot of food and see the New Year in at midnight with a glass of champagne. Children wait for Father Frost and the Snow Maiden to bring presents. Because of the long winter break, many people travel or visit their relatives.

Victory Day on the ninth of May is a much more serious occasion. It commemorates the victory over Nazi Germany in the Second World War. There is a military parade on Red Square, and people lay flowers at war memorials. Many families walk through the streets with photographs of relatives who fought in the war.

Maslenitsa, which takes place a week before Lent, is a cheerful festival. It is a way to say goodbye to winter. People bake pancakes, take part in street games and sing songs, and on the last day they burn a straw figure of winter. It is a holiday for the whole family, and children love it.

Different as they are, all three holidays bring people together.

Текст авторский по материалам «Russian holidays» / «Holidays in Russia» (на проверку); озвучка синтезатором речи.

Step 2 · Understand the text

Choose the best answer. The explanation appears at once.

1. Which holiday is described as the most popular?

The text says: “New Year is the most popular holiday of the year.”

2. Why do many people travel at New Year?

“Because of the long winter break, many people travel…”

3. What do people do on Victory Day?

“people lay flowers at war memorials”

4. What is Maslenitsa a way to do?

“It is a way to say goodbye to winter.”

5. What do the three holidays have in common?

The last sentence: “all three holidays bring people together.”

Step 5 · Speak and write

Chunk bank: see the New Year in · put up a tree · bring presents · commemorate the victory · lay flowers at a war memorial · take part in · say goodbye to winter · bring people together · the whole family · a military parade

Exam question (Speaking, Задание 3): “What is your favourite public holiday? Why?” Give a full answer in 2–3 sentences, about 40 seconds. Use at least two chunks from the bank.

Now write 5–6 sentences about a holiday in your family. Use at least five chunks.

Check: did you say when it is celebrated, what people do, why it matters to you?
